```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(REPS)
```

## A separate hub with familiar output

`calculate_spar()` calculates sales price appraisal ratio (SPAR) indices from
transaction prices and matched appraisal values. It does not fit a hedonic
regression. As with `calculate_hedonic_index()`, one method returns a data.frame;
multiple methods return a named list in the requested order. Method names are
case-insensitive and repeated names are calculated once.

The public interface is:

```r
calculate_spar(
  dataset, method, period_variable, dependent_variable, appraisal_variable,
  grouping_variables, index_type_variable = NULL,
  reference_period_pattern = "01$", chained = FALSE,
  base_value = 100, month_modulo = 100, parallel = FALSE
)
```

Column arguments are strings. `grouping_variables` defines each short-term
series, usually by appraisal vintage and property type. `index_type_variable`
identifies the independent series to chain, such as property type or property
type and region; it must be a subset of the grouping columns. There is no
additional `type_variable` argument.

## Three variants, one sample of complete pairs

For each period/group, with transaction price `p` and appraisal value `a`:

| Method | Period ratio |
|:--|:--|
| `"arithmetic"` | `mean(p) / mean(a)` |
| `"geometric"` | `exp(mean(log(p))) / exp(mean(log(a)))` |
| `"unweighted"` | `mean(p / a)` |

If either side of a pair is missing, both sides are excluded for that
observation. In particular, an appraisal with a missing transaction price does
not enter the arithmetic or geometric denominator. Unused columns do not affect
the sample. Observed prices and appraisals must be finite and strictly positive.
A retained period/group without any complete pair is an error.

This small example can be calculated by hand:

```{r manual-data}
example <- data.frame(
  month = rep(c(202101, 202102), each = 2),
  vintage = 2019, type = "A",
  price = c(100, 300, 200, 600),
  appraisal = c(100, 200, 100, 300)
)
results <- calculate_spar(
  example, c("arithmetic", "geometric", "unweighted"),
  period_variable = "month", dependent_variable = "price",
  appraisal_variable = "appraisal", grouping_variables = c("vintage", "type")
)
lapply(results, function(x) x[c("period", "ratio_numerator", "growth_rate", "Index")])
```

The January ratios are `4/3`, `sqrt(1.5)`, and `1.25`; all February ratios are 2.
Thus the February indices are 150, approximately 163.30, and 160. These variants
need not agree because they weight transaction/appraisal relationships
differently.

## References and identifiers

Within each grouping series:

```text
growth_rate = current period ratio / reference period ratio
Index       = 100 * growth_rate                 (unchained)
```

`reference_period_pattern` is a regular expression, not a REPS reference-year
prefix. The default `"01$"` selects January in YYYYMM periods. `"Q1$"` works for
unchained quarterly character periods such as `"2021Q1"`.

The regex must match at most one distinct period per group. Multiple matches
are an error. A group without a matching reference is warned about and omitted;
if none remain, the result is an empty data.frame with the regular output
columns. Missing/blank period or grouping identifiers are rejected rather than
treated as separate series. Column roles must be distinct; grouping columns
must not conflict with standardized output names such as `period` or `Index`.

## Chaining and its boundary assumption

Chaining follows the newer SPAR development convention and is separate from
hedonic annual-overlap chaining. `month_modulo` defines numeric segments, with
a start where `period %% month_modulo == 1`. With YYYYMM, use 100. Numeric YYYYQ
quarters can use 10 with a reference pattern of `"1$"`. Character labels such
as `"2021Q1"` are supported only for unchained calculation.

Each short-term grouping series must lie within one numeric segment and begin
at its reference period, which must be the segment start. Independent chained
series must have at most one aggregated row for each numeric period; ambiguous
overlapping appraisal vintages require an explicit data selection before
chaining. All chain arguments are validated even when chaining is disabled.

For a short-term normalized ratio `g`, the applied factor is:

| Position | Growth factor |
|:--|:--|
| First observation in an independent series | 1 |
| First observation of a later segment | `g` |
| Other observations | `g / previous_g` |

The index is `base_value * cumprod(growth_factor)`. At a reference segment start,
`g = 1`, so the previous endpoint is carried forward unchanged. This **assumes
no movement at the boundary**: the calculation does not infer an unobserved
December-to-January change or a valuation bridge. Use it only when that linking
convention is appropriate; it is not an estimate of missing cross-vintage
information. Gaps within a segment compare the available observations.

```{r manual-chain}
chain_data <- data.frame(
  month = c(202101, 202112, 202201, 202202),
  vintage = c(2019, 2019, 2020, 2020), type = "A",
  price = c(100, 120, 300, 330), appraisal = 100
)
chain_result <- calculate_spar(
  chain_data, "arithmetic", period_variable = "month",
  dependent_variable = "price", appraisal_variable = "appraisal",
  grouping_variables = c("vintage", "type"),
  chained = TRUE, index_type_variable = "type"
)
chain_result[c("period", "growth_rate", "growth_factor", "Index")]
```

The short-term ratios are `1, 1.2, 1, 1.1`; the factors are `1, 1.2, 1, 1.1`;
the chained levels are **100, 120, 120, 132**. The raw price increase from 120 to
300 across vintages is not used as a measured price change. Every independent
index-type series is initialized at `base_value` separately.

## Packaged example, parallel methods, and plotting

`aritmethic_data` retains the established dataset name from SPAR development.
It contains 360 transactions, two appraisal vintages, five property types,
and twelve monthly periods per vintage. Non-syntactic names are passed as strings.

```{r packaged-data}
data("aritmethic_data")
str(aritmethic_data)
spar <- calculate_spar(
  dataset = aritmethic_data,
  method = c("arithmetic", "geometric", "unweighted"),
  period_variable = "Period", dependent_variable = "Price",
  appraisal_variable = "Appraisal Value",
  grouping_variables = c("Appraisal Year", "Property Type"),
  chained = TRUE, index_type_variable = "Property Type"
)
names(spar)
```

For multiple methods, `parallel = TRUE` uses the same optional task helper as
hedonic indices. The output has the same content as sequential calculation;
small datasets often benefit more from avoiding worker startup costs.

Every frame contains character `period`, `Index`, all grouping identifiers,
`ratio_numerator`, `ratio_denominator`, and `growth_rate`. Arithmetic/geometric
output also preserves the aggregated price and appraisal components as
`numerator_numerator` and `numerator_denominator`. Chained output additionally
contains `chaining_true_false` and `growth_factor`.

Grouped output must be filtered to one series before plotting. Otherwise
`plot_price_index()` raises a clear error instead of joining unrelated series.

```{r plot-spar, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
plot_series <- lapply(spar, function(x) x[x[["Property Type"]] == "A", ])
plot_price_index(plot_series, title = "SPAR comparison: property type A")
```
